data.title: Luca Van Assche's Polymarket Odds for Rolex Paris Masters Match Drop 18%
data.description: On Polymarket, the “Luca Van Assche” option in the Rolex Paris Masters match market against Rinky Hijikata fell to 46.5% from 64.5% one hour earlier, a drop of 18%. According to ChainCatcher, the odds were monitored on the prediction market.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Microsoft Gradually Ends Deals to Rent AI Cloud Capacity From Oracle
data.description: According to Jin10, market sources say Microsoft (MSFT.O) is gradually ending deals related to renting AI cloud computing capacity from Oracle (ORCL.N).

data.title: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar Says Midterm Results Will Not Change Data Center Investment Plans
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CNBC, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said on Friday that the company’s AI infrastructure investment plans would not change based on the U.S. midterm election results. OpenAI will continue working with major hyperscale cloud providers and use financing to meet customer demand for AI. Friar said the election outcome would not significantly affect the business, while the company would step up engagement with local communities and work to build trust as data centers receive more attention.

In the midterms, only one of 41 local data center-related ballot measures across 10 states did not support restricting construction or opposing measures in favor of development. Voters’ main concerns included higher electricity bills, environmental damage and effects on employment.

Friar said OpenAI confidentially filed an IPO application with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in June and is considering a 2027 listing. The company is also discussing a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation. She said demand for AI is real and continues to grow.

data.title: Nvidia, Moderna, IonQ, Airbnb and Firefly Aerospace Lead Midday Stock Moves
data.description: According to CNBC, Nvidia rebounded more than 3% Friday, returning to positive territory for 2026. Moderna gained 7% after beating third-quarter earnings estimates and raising its 2026 revenue growth outlook to 15% to 25%, from no more than 10%. IonQ rose 17% after lifting its full-year revenue guidance to $505 million to $515 million, above analysts’ $456.2 million estimate. Airbnb jumped 11% as third-quarter earnings of $3.16 per share and revenue of $4.87 billion topped estimates. Firefly Aerospace surged nearly 30% after announcing a roughly $1.3 billion agreement with AST SpaceMobile to provide 36 rocket engines and license the engines’ intellectual property.

data.title: Canada Plans One-Time Permanent Residency for Up to 200,000 Temporary Residents
data.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government plans to grant permanent residency to as many as 200,000 temporary residents by the end of 2027, in addition to its annual immigration target, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: CoreWeave Bond Yield Tops 16% as AI Debt Costs Rise
data.description: According to CNBC, the yield on CoreWeave’s 2032 bond, which carries a 9.625% coupon, climbed above 16%. The company’s five-year credit default swaps rose above 1,289 basis points Thursday, surpassing their October peak, then eased 8% Friday to about 1,155, according to Deutsche Bank. Credit default swap spreads on Nvidia, Broadcom and Amazon.com rose 76%, 49% and 44%, respectively, over the last month, but remained low in absolute terms.

data.title: Apollo’s Brightspeed in Talks With Creditors for Multibillion-Dollar Funding
data.description: Brightspeed and its creditors are in talks over a multibillion-dollar funding lifeline as the broadband provider grapples with heavy debt amid its capital-intensive fiber internet rollout, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Donald Trump: Only “Stupid” Leaders Say No to AI
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump reiterated his support for artificial intelligence after concerns that the technology could face tighter regulation triggered a stock market plunge that wiped out $2.3 trillion in market value. According to Sina Finance, Trump said on social media of AI companies, “They are gold, and only ‘stupid’ leaders would say no to the wealth they bring.”

data.title: Core Scientific Sells 816 BTC, Holds 32 BTC
data.description: Core Scientific sold 816 BTC and now holds 32 BTC, according to a post by Bitcoin Treasuries on X. According to Odaily, the publicly listed Bitcoin miner sold the BTC to meet capital expenditures and other cash needs and is transitioning to building AI data centers.

data.title: Elon Musk: Government Contracts to Account for Under 10% of SpaceX Revenue This Quarter
data.description: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk wrote on X that revenue from the government will account for less than 10% of SpaceX’s revenue this quarter and less than 5% a year later. According to Sina Finance, Musk said he would be happy to cancel any contract the U.S. government does not want.

data.title: Kazuo Ueda: Corporate Risk Appetite Appears to Be Recovering
data.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda focused on the modern history of Japan’s current account surplus in a speech on Friday and did not directly comment on monetary policy. According to Sina Finance, Ueda spoke at the International Monetary Fund on “Japan’s Current Account Surplus and Corporate Adjustment,” saying bank loan growth recently exceeded 5%, its fastest pace in 30 years, and that corporate risk appetite appeared to be recovering with the return of moderate inflation. He said Japan’s current account surplus had shown significant resilience. He also said Japan had a large stock of net foreign assets, while returns on overseas investment remained substantially higher than those on domestic investment.

data.title: AI | Brookfield’s Connor Teskey Says Community Buy-In Is Key to AI Growth
data.description: Brookfield Asset Management CEO Connor Teskey said local community support is crucial before construction of artificial intelligence infrastructure, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI CFO Confirms Financing Talks at Valuation Nearly 50% Above March Round
data.description: OpenAI’s chief financial officer confirmed that the company is in financing talks at a valuation nearly 50% higher than that of its funding round completed in March. According to Odaily, CNBC reported the confirmation.

data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI CFO: Company Will Continue Investing in AI Data Centers
data.description:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said Friday that the company will continue investing in AI infrastructure despite voter opposition to data center development in the midterm elections. According to Sina Finance, Friar said at the Citi TMT Industry Leaders Conference in Pebble Beach, California, that OpenAI had partnered early with major hyperscalers and would continue fundraising to meet customer needs.

Ballotpedia data and additional results compiled Wednesday showed that, among 41 local ballot measures across 10 states, only one failed to advance restrictions; voters in the others backed limits on construction or rejected pro-development proposals. Opponents have raised concerns about environmental damage, higher utility bills, and potential job losses.

Friar said the election would not fundamentally change OpenAI’s approach, and that the company would continue working with local communities to build trust. Investors have recently grown more cautious toward AI stocks amid rising borrowing costs, concerns about mounting debt, and public opposition to the AI industry. On Thursday, the Nasdaq posted its steepest one-day drop in 19 months, with chipmakers and new cloud operators closely tied to AI infrastructure leading the declines.

data.title: Kazuo Ueda: Japan’s Underlying Inflation Reaches 2% for First Time in Decades
data.description: According to Jin10, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said underlying inflation has reached 2% for the first time in decades.

data.title: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda: Much Work Remains on Inflation
data.description: According to Jin10, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said his overall view on inflation is that much work remains to be done.

data.title: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda: Wage Growth Matches 2% Target; “We Are in Equilibrium”
data.description: According to Jin10, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said wage growth is consistent with the 2% inflation target and that “we are in an equilibrium state.”

data.title: STOCKS | Chipmakers Rebound as Strong Data Weighs on Bonds
data.description:
Chipmakers rebounded, lifting Wall Street, while strong economic readings weighed on bonds and reinforced speculation that the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, Bloomberg reported.

Max Kettner, HSBC’s chief multi-asset strategist, said the AI trade is following market narratives rather than fundamentals.

data.title: ECB Succession Likely to Come Down to Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos
data.description: The contest to succeed European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will probably come down to Dutchman Klaas Knot and Spaniard Pablo Hernandez de Cos, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Pimco's Tiffany Wilding Says Multiple Fed Hikes Are Reasonable
data.description: Pimco economist Tiffany Wilding said the US employment report did not change her outlook for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, according to Bloomberg. Speaking on “Bloomberg Open Interest,” she said another increase in March is possible and described the moves as a policy recalibration.
